chapter_summary: A failed sketch stays visible beside the finished passage. She keeps it as evidence that the work has a history.

spatality.place: the wall between two panels, one finished and one spoiled
spatality.season: the hour before dawn, dry season
spatality.route: from the failed study to the finished passage and back
spatality.texture: flaking skin of dried lime, a smear that will not lift, cold hands

poetic_parameters.movement: Confessionalism — unflinching exposure of personal failure, kept in the first person and never excused.
writing_skills: visceral physical imagery of the failed work
a closing admission rather than a moral
poetic_parameters.image_seed: a spoiled panel left beside a finished one, its smear already dry
poetic_parameters.volta: from wanting to scrape the failure off to deciding to leave it where it is
poetic_parameters.sonic_texture: the wet consonants of smear, scrape, spoil, and the flatness of the repeated word again
poetic_parameters.line_gesture: winding, slightly breathless lines that keep doubling back, ending on a short flat line
poetic_parameters.variety_note: Chapter seven refused a line before making it; this poem makes the line, ruins it, and keeps the ruin — the first time failure is displayed rather than avoided.
poetic_parameters.metaphor_family: stain, scar, and evidence kept instead of cleaned
poetic_parameters.address: the failed sketch, then the self in the same breath
poetic_parameters.closing_move: an admission that the failure is now part of the work, offered without relief
